summary: The Optiq is the cheapest way into General Motors' relaunched Cadillac brand in Australia, and reviewers consistently praise its distinctive, well-finished cabin, quiet running and unusually generous standard equipment for $80,000 before on-road costs. The consensus criticism is just as consistent: 425km of WLTP range and a 110kW DC charging ceiling are the weakest numbers among luxury mid-size electric SUVs on sale here, and Australia takes the superseded 224kW powertrain rather than the US car's 328kW update. Opinion divides mainly on the ride: CarExpert finds it composed but short of the plushness the badge implies on 21-inch wheels, while CarsGuide's August 2026 review calls it very comfortable.
pros: $80,000 before on-road costs for a single, fully loaded grade, under the $91,661 fuel-efficient LCT threshold that governs the novated-lease FBT exemption today (but above the $75,000 cap that applies from 1 April 2027)
Generous rear cabin: a 2954mm wheelbase that reviewers rate for near-limousine rear knee room, with a quiet, active-noise-cancelled interior CarsGuide calls serene

Heavily specified in its single grade — 33-inch curved display with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto (features GM deleted from its US EVs), 19-speaker AKG Dolby Atmos audio, heated/ventilated/massaging front seats, Brembo front brakes, panoramic glass roof and 21-inch wheels
22.1kW three-phase AC charging is unusually quick for the segment and adds roughly 100km of range per hour at home, which softens the weak DC rate for overnight chargers
Five-year unlimited-kilometre warranty with no servicing strings attached, an eight-year/160,000km battery warranty, and a five-star Euro NCAP result (2025) scoring 83% for adult occupant protection
cons: 110kW peak DC charging and 425km of WLTP range rank last among luxury mid-size electric SUVs sold here (a Polestar 4 accepts 200kW), and the 19.9kWh/100km WLTP claim is high for the class (CarsGuide measured 21.2kWh/100km)

The boot is smaller than local spec sheets suggest: 443 litres to the cover on the European VDA measure (1340 litres folded to the roof), behind the BMW iX1's 490 and Polestar 4's 526; the 744 litres quoted in Australia is the US to-the-roof figure

Australia gets the superseded 224kW/480Nm dual-motor drivetrain while the US MY26 car has 328kW/675Nm and 150kW charging, and GM Australia has given no timing for bringing the update here; the Optiq-V is ruled out entirely

Firm-riding on 21-inch wheels with no adaptive dampers available, which several Australian reviewers judged short of the plushness a luxury badge implies, and the steering is described as vague on-centre

New-brand ownership risk: Cadillac does not report Australian sales, retails through a handful of metropolitan experience centres, permanently cut the larger Lyriq's price by $32,000 during 2026, and had still not confirmed Optiq service pricing at launch
